markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (96%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set and high reliability, but the second model disagrees and tumor-nucleus fraction is high.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 96%, Normal 3%, InSitu 2% | Strongly favors Benign |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.98 / 88th percentile | Not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Disagrees on top class |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Benign | Nearest match is Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 5, 10) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Weak
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 1) · ↓ invasive · Scored below typical, so it lowers invasive association [F2] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 10) · ↓ invasive · Scored low; small pull away from invasive · Validated
- **Tumor-nucleus fraction** (regions 0, 1, 9) · context · 96th percentile tumor-nuclei fraction; mean nuclear size lowest in reference [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions lowers the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect classifier use. Mitotic figures (0/20) is Unreliable [F4].

## Could be wrong if
- The second model (MUSK) disagrees on top class, so the Benign call may not be robust.
- Tumor-nucleus fraction exceeds 96% of benign/normal references, which sits uneasily with a Benign call.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 1, 9:** Confirm the HoVer-Net neoplastic nuclei are truly atypical, given the Benign call.
2. **Regions 1, 5, 10:** Verify gland/tubule architecture and absence of infiltrating stroma.
3. **Region 7:** Review duct-confined atypical cells; concept is Weak (12/20).
